html:
The Democratic Republic of Georgia was the first modern Georgian state, declared in Tbilisi on 26 May 1918 after the Transcaucasian federation broke up, and led by the Mensheviks, the moderate wing of Russian Marxism.

Under Noe Zhordania it held elections, carried out land reform and gave women the vote. Germany and then Britain offered protection. Soviet Russia recognised its independence in 1920, but in February 1921 the Red Army invaded, and Tbilisi fell within weeks. The government fled to France. A revolt in 1924 was crushed with thousands executed. Georgia became a Soviet republic, ruled in the 1930s by Stalin, himself a Georgian. Its flag was taken up again in 1990, and the Rose Revolution replaced it in 2004.
